overview_markdown:
## Overview

thepopebot is a self-hosted personal AI agent platform that combines chat, coding agents, and live terminal workspaces into a single application. It positions itself as 'your personal agent, coding environment, and communication platform — all in one app,' supporting any LLM (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, and more).

The architecture centers on a 'Brain' event handler with three entry points: a browser-based chat, Telegram integration (with per-user verification), and live coding workspaces where you can attach a terminal to a running container. It distinguishes between **live chat** (quick questions, streaming responses in-process) and **agent jobs** (background workers that run in fresh Docker containers, open PRs, auto-merge, and DM you when done). Configuration is stored in SQLite with AES-encrypted secrets, and recent commits show active hardening — removing stale config caches and adding flexible Telegram webhook overrides.

Compared to OpenClaw, thepopebot is a much smaller, single-maintainer project with a narrower integration surface (Telegram today, Slack/Discord promised) but a focused, opinionated workflow around coding agents and PR automation. It runs entirely on your own hardware with your own tokens, making it a privacy-friendly option for developers who want a simple, unified agent environment without the scale or ecosystem of OpenClaw.
